report: Hussain T, ..., Aldaz CM. Wwox deletion leads to reduced GABA-ergic inhibitory interneuron numbers and activation of microglia and astrocytes in mouse hippocampus. Neurobiol Dis 2019 (epub 2018-10-02; ppub 2019-01; pp163-176). THIS is the item the repository calls "Aldaz 2019": a full paper, not a poster.
measured: (1) number of PV-immunopositive cells, optical-fractionator stereology; (2) number of NPY-immunopositive cells; (3) GAD65/67 protein by western blot of whole hippocampus; (4) IBA-1 and GFAP area fraction; (5) RNA-seq of hippocampal neurospheres from newborns (283 DE genes) and qRT-PCR of hippocampus
readout_level: tissue (marker-positive cell number per animal; homogenate protein; culture transcripts)
region: hippocampus: dentate gyrus, CA1, CA3 and whole hippocampus (PV, NPY); whole-hippocampus homogenate (GAD); no cortex measurement of PV/NPY
genotype_and_control: global Wwox KO (BK5-Cre oocyte recombination of floxed allele, mixed 129SV/C57Bl/6) vs littermate controls (Methods 2.1: "As controls we used ... littermates"; genotype symbols are stripped in the extracted text)
n_and_unit_of_n: PV: KO n=7, WT n=7 (animals; the counts are per-animal stereological estimates); NPY: n=6 v 6; GAD65/67 blot n=5 v 5; qRT-PCR hippocampus n=4 v 4; neurospheres: sample numbers not read in the text (the repo records 2 v 3)
exact_result_verbatim_quote_and_locator: Results 3.1: "Stereological quantification indicated that [KO] mice displayed a statistically significant reduction in the total number of PV+ interneurons in the DG region (p < .005,) and CA1 subfield (p < .05,)"; "The overall reduction of PV+ interneurons in [KO] mice amounted to 44% when the hippocampus was taken in its entirety (p < .005,)"; "Some hippocampal areas in [KO] mice showed a complete absence of such cells". CA3 is described only as "significantly low" in the text and is not given a p value in the text. NPY: "a 30% reduction in the total number of NPY+ interneurons" in DG (p < .05), "CA1 and CA3 subfields, did not exhibit any obvious difference". Results 3.4: "significantly lower levels of GAD65/67 protein expression" (p < .05). Methods 2.3: primary antibodies "anti-PV, anti-NPY, anti-IBA-1, or anti-GFAP" (no NeuN, no pan-GABAergic lineage marker). Methods 2.4: counts "for the DG, CA1 and CA3 subfields". Discussion: "may induce hippocampal hyperexcitability" (hypothesis, not tested). Extraction note: text from NCBI efetch XML, Fig panels not viewed.
explanations_CAN_separate: (a)+(b)+(c) together are the only thing it can show: fewer cells carrying PV immunoreactivity at 2 weeks in a null. It CAN show that marker-positive number is lower and region-specific (NPY lower in DG only; PV lower in DG and CA1).
explanations_CANNOT_separate: (a) cannot be told from (b) or (c): the count estimates cells carrying the stain; no death, lineage, birth-dating, pan-GABAergic (Gad1/VGAT/GAD67 per cell) or pan-neuronal denominator; 2 weeks is inside the PV/PNN maturation window, so delay (c) is not excluded; (d) no function measured (GAD65/67 in homogenate is protein, not GABA release). A systemic null at 2 weeks (hypoglycaemia etc. known in the null) cannot separate cell-autonomous from secondary injury (INFERENZA).

region: neocortex layer II/III (sIPSC, interneuron properties, bursts); hippocampus CA1/CA3 (evoked field only)

genotype_and_control: Synapsin-I-Cre x Wwox flox/flox neuron-specific KO (S-KO, Cre+ fl/fl) vs Cre+ littermates S-WT and S-HT; for sEPSC/sIPSC S-WT and S-HT pooled as S-CTL
n_and_unit_of_n: sIPSC (Fig 4H legend): "S-CTLs n = 14 cells from 7 animals; S-KOs n = 9 cells from 5 animals; s-WT N = 7 cells, 4 animals; s-HET N = 7 cells, 4 animals" (components give 8 animals, not 7); interneurons Table 1 N cells/animals: control 5/4, KO 6/5; tests: KS test on event distributions (unit not declared; p values down to 1e-135)
exact_result_verbatim_quote_and_locator: Results (Fig 4): "the sIPSCs were reduced in both amplitude and frequency (Fig. 4G, H; mean amplitude: S-CTLs 57.3 ± 31.0pA; S-KOs 27.5 ± 19.4 pA; mean frequency S-CTL 10.3 ± 11.5 Hz; S-KOs 8.4 ± 10.0 Hz)". Results (properties): "For the interneurons, only the action potential amplitude was diminished in the S-KOs compared to the controls"; Table 1 interneuron AP amplitude 60.78 ± 3.31 vs 45.03 ± 3.58 (*). Methods: "For recordings of sIPSCs, a high-chloride intracellular solution was used" (140 KCl); "Putative pyramidal neurons were identified based on their appearance under the infrared filter"; no PV identification procedure for interneurons. Discussion: "these findings may indicate a change in pre- or post-synaptic properties unrelated to action potential firing, or reflect a WWOX-dependent decrease in the interneuron population (Hussain et al., 2019) for which we did not account." Hippocampus: "neocortical hyperexcitability ... was not observed in the hippocampal circuitry, with one notable exception" (CA1-to-CA3 PS amplitude up). explanations_CAN_separate: CAN show (d)-type readout: a reduced spontaneous inhibitory drive onto pyramidal cells in L2/3 at P13-P17, with interneuron firing frequency-current slope not different and spike amplitude lower. It CAN say the circuit output is lower in this model/region/age.
explanations_CANNOT_separate: CANNOT separate (a) loss of PV cells from (b) marker loss, (c) delay or (d) release/receptor change: no PV identification, no counts, no marker; sIPSC mixes all interneuron classes and firing-dependent release; no mIPSC so pre/post not split; 140 mM KCl pipette does not give physiological E_Cl; sample counts inconsistent in the legend; KS test on events not animals.
